thread:
mei: heads-up: our new quantized bring-up (horizon-int6-v1) is producing intermittent structured-output failures when streaming. ~0.75% parse_fail over last 2k calls. logs show suffix truncation and occasional duplicated commas.

rahul: is this only streaming? what's batch look like?

mei: batch-mode is 0.09%. fp16-streaming baseline 0.04%. streaming+int6 is worst. small excerpt saved: 
```
{"op":"create_incident","meta":{"desc":"node OOM","tags":["infra","urgent"},]
```
stream cut before closing array/brace.

zane: that trailing ",]" is suspicious. could be chunk boundary cutting inside a multi-byte token or a quant decoder rounding that alters tokenization.

rahul: can we reproduce deterministically? run canary harness with fixed seed, streaming vs buffered, and capture raw chunks + token indices. also mirror to fp16 for token-level diff.

mei: scheduling a 5k run now with temp=0, top_p=1.0, seed fixed. saving per-chunk sha256 and token_idx metadata. snippet I used to dump chunks:

```python
c = Client(model="horizon-int6-v1", stream=True, seed=42)
for i, p in enumerate(load('toolcall-heavy')):
  r = c.generate(p)
  write_raw(i, r.raw_chunks, r.token_indices)
```

ci-bot: canary job queued: /ci/canary/1758888888/5k. will publish report to /ci/reports/1758888888.json.

zane: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) streaming stitcher that waits up to TTL=140ms for syntactic close and performs minimal repairs (trim trailing commas, append missing single brace if counts mismatch by 1); 2) for canary, disable retry-on-parse-fail to avoid duplicate tool invocations; 3) route large payloads (>1k bytes) to buffered delivery mode.

rahul: add metric 'stitcher_fix_ratio' and 'stitcher_latency_penalty' so we can track impact. also log a diff flag when the stitcher alters output.

mei: if token-level diffs show divergence before transport (i.e., checksums differ vs fp16 at same token index), that means generation distortion: try per-channel scale quant variant and mixed-precision last-4-layers. we'll need a small bench matrix for latency/cost tradeoffs.

zane: if diffs are only at or after transport, infra should look at framing and chunk concat logic. we should capture raw bytes and any utf-8 decode errors.

ops: temporarily paused streaming rollout for horizon-int6-v1 and switched to buffered fallback for canary. turned off auto-retry for funcall parser.

ci-bot: report posted: /ci/reports/1758888888.json (streaming_parse_fail:0.74%, buffered:0.10%, stitcher_auto_fixed:0.30%, duplicate_invokes:+0.5pp). token_checksum_divergence_median: 48 on failing cases.

rahul: divergence at token ~48 suggests quant generation effect. I'll start an ablation grid: variants = [per-channel, last-4-mp, clamp-tweak]. will run small 1k jobs and report parse_fail + p95 latency + cost.

mei: thanks. created ticket INF-4012 assigned to @rahul and @zane. we'll reconvene after ablation results. :thumbsup:
